headline: Messi plays his last Argentina match, ending a 21-year international career
facts: ESPN reports Messi played his final Argentina match on 6 October 2026, a friendly win over Benin, scoring a penalty.
Messi's last official match was the 1-0 World Cup final loss to Spain; ESPN gives his farewell numbers as 208 appearances and 126 goals (a second ESPN piece says 207 caps and 125 goals).
Messi will return to Argentina on 19 January 2027 with Inter Miami for a friendly against River Plate at the Monumental.
background: Messi captained Argentina to the 2022 World Cup and two Copa America titles, and he is still playing club football for Inter Miami in MLS.

headline: Argentina lose 1-2 to Uruguay in first game without Messi, Scaloni leaves No. 10 empty
facts: Uruguay won 2-1 at La Bombonera on 13 November; Balerdi scored an own goal and Maxi Araujo added a second, Alvarez replied for Argentina.
It was Argentina's first match since Messi's retirement, and Scaloni left the No. 10 shirt unassigned.
Uruguay are now coached by Diego Forlan, and Scaloni said Argentina must rebuild.
background: Scaloni has coached Argentina since 2018 and won the 2022 World Cup and two Copa America titles with Messi at the centre of the team.

headline: Argentina thrash Costa Rica 7-0 as Nico Paz and Alvarez both score twice
facts: Argentina won 7-0 in Cordoba; Paz and Alvarez each scored twice before halftime for a 4-0 lead.
Mastantuono scored twice (48', 88') and Mac Allister once.
The win came three days after the 2-1 loss to Uruguay, the first game after Messi's retirement.
background: Paz plays for Como and is being tipped as the heir to Messi's No. 10 shirt; Mastantuono is on loan at Fiorentina from Real Madrid, per ESPN.

headline: Ronaldo retires from Portugal after row with Jorge Jesus, Portugal then lose 1-4 to Denmark
facts: ESPN says Ronaldo, 41, quit international football after a falling out with coach Jorge Jesus over playing time; another ESPN piece dates the announcement to 5 November.
Denmark won 4-1 in Braga on 14 November, Portugal's heaviest competitive home defeat, with Hojlund scoring twice.
The home crowd whistled and chanted for Ronaldo during the game.
background: Ronaldo is Portugal's all-time top scorer with 146 goals in 234 appearances, and he plays club football for Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia, where Jesus once coached him.

headline: Ronaldo's mother says she is glad Portugal lost and blasts the tribute to her son
facts: Before the Denmark game the federation had every Portugal player wear a No. 7 shirt as a tribute, but Ronaldo did not attend.
Dolores Aveiro said her son felt deceived and not respected, and said the Denmark defeat was deserved.
Jorge Jesus answered at a press conference, calling her an exemplary mother and Ronaldo a Portuguese legend.
background: Ronaldo started his senior career at Sporting CP, where his mother said a separate tribute will be held for him.
footage_terms: Jorge Jesus press conference Ronaldo mother

headline: Portugal win 3-2 at Wales as Carlos Forbs scores in the Ronaldo-honouring No. 7 shirt
facts: Portugal beat Wales 3-2 in Cardiff in the Nations League, their first win since Ronaldo's retirement.
Carlos Forbs, 22, scored the 70th-minute winner, his first goal for Portugal, wearing No. 7 with a line through the number.
Pedro Neto, the Chelsea winger, was sent off for two reckless tackles in two minutes.
background: Forbs plays for Club Brugge, and Portugal finished top of their group with five wins from six games.
footage_terms: Pedro Neto red card Wales Portugal

headline: Pochettino leaves USMNT for Manchester United after emotional 2-0 farewell win over Haiti
facts: Pochettino's last USMNT game was a 2-0 win over Haiti in Cincinnati (8-0 on aggregate) with a Pulisic bicycle kick and a goal from Julian Hall.
He left less than three months after signing a new U.S. Soccer contract, and about half his staff, including assistant Jesus Perez, followed him to Manchester.
Fans chanted his name and the stadium played Country Roads after the final whistle.
background: Pochettino previously managed Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea, and took the USMNT job in 2024.

headline: Bruce Arena says U.S. Soccer has no clue how to replace Pochettino
facts: Arena, now with the San Jose Earthquakes, said the federation does not know what it is doing in its search.
He opposed hiring Pochettino in 2025, arguing a foreign coach cannot understand a national team's culture.
U23 coach Steve Cherundolo will lead a December camp and a friendly against Jamaica.
background: Arena is a former U.S. national team coach and was among the strongest voices for hiring domestic coaches.

headline: Rafael Marquez finally wins as Mexico coach, Tecatito Corona ends a four-year goal drought
facts: Mexico beat Jamaica 1-0 in Monterrey and went through 3-3 on away goals after a 3-2 first-leg defeat.
It was Marquez's first win in charge after going 0-3-2 in his first five matches.
Corona scored his first international goal since September 2021, and Mexico now face the United States in the Nations League semifinal at SoFi Stadium in March 2027.
background: Marquez, a former Mexico captain, took over from Javier Aguirre after the World Cup, and Mexico are the defending Nations League champions.
footage_terms: Mexico Jamaica Nations League Corona goal
Mexico vs USA Nations League semifinal

headline: Infantino apologises over the plan to sell a stake in FIFA tournaments, English FA still wants him out
facts: FIFA had planned to sell a 20% stake in future tournaments to private investors via a new company, FIFA Forward Enterprise, valued at $20bn.
At a FIFA Council meeting in Zurich Infantino apologised for not informing the council earlier; the plan was dropped after pushback from UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC.
FA chair Debbie Hewitt said he is not fit to be president without answering the council's questions, and the FIFA Peace Prize given to Trump in December 2025 is likely to be scrapped.
background: Infantino has led FIFA since 2016 and is seeking a fourth term in March 2027.

headline: Japan's Kohzo Tashima becomes first challenger to Infantino for the FIFA presidency
facts: Tashima, a FIFA Council member and former JFA president, declared his candidacy on 5 November and is the first Japanese person to run for FIFA president.
He says he is open to joining forces with Diallo, though they have not yet spoken.
The vote is on 18 March; an unofficial AP count puts Infantino at 105 votes, one short of the 106 needed in a two-candidate race.
background: Infantino was expected to win a fourth term unopposed before the World Cup stake-sale row, and the Asian Football Confederation has endorsed him.

headline: France federation boss Philippe Diallo confirms bid to unseat Infantino
facts: Diallo, 63, was put forward by UEFA's executive committee and says he needs 106 of 211 votes at the March vote in Rabat.
French President Macron backs him, and France withdrew an earlier letter of support for Infantino in September.
UEFA is pursuing legal action in U.S. courts and seeking evidence for a possible Swiss criminal complaint, which FIFA calls a smear campaign.
background: Diallo became interim French federation president in January 2023 and later joined UEFA's executive committee.

headline: Klopp says FIFA under Infantino is worse than under Blatter
facts: Germany coach Klopp said he hopes Infantino is replaced and called the situation at FIFA worse than under Sepp Blatter.
Critics also point to FIFA's handling of a red card for USA striker Folarin Balogun that let him play against Belgium at the World Cup.
The election is on 18 March 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.
background: Klopp managed Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool before taking over Germany; Blatter was banned from football in 2015 over a payment to Michel Platini.

headline: Spanish FA chief insists the 2030 World Cup final can only be played in Spain
facts: Spanish federation president Rafael Louzan said the final can and will only be held in Spain, the reigning champion's home.
FIFA has not chosen the venue; Morocco wants its planned 115,000-seat King Hassan II Stadium, and Portugal reportedly lacks an 80,000-capacity ground.
Opposition leader Feijoo said Spain should withdraw as host if it does not get the final, and Louzan expects no decision until 2028.
background: The 2030 tournament opens in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay before moving to Spain, Portugal and Morocco.
footage_terms: 2030 World Cup final venue Spain Morocco

headline: Harry Kane wins the Ballon d'Or, England's first winner in 25 years
facts: Kane, 33, won the 2026 Ballon d'Or, the first Englishman to win it since Michael Owen in 2001 and only the fifth English winner.
He scored 73 goals in all competitions last season, 61 of them for Bayern.
About ten days later he signed a new three-year deal with Bayern running to 2029.
background: Kane began his senior career with loans at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester, became Tottenham's all-time top scorer and joined Bayern in 2023 for about 100 million pounds.

headline: England hammer Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka, Kane scores twice and nears Shilton's cap record
facts: England won 7-0 on 3 October; Kane scored twice, Saka twice, with Bellingham, Gordon and Rogers also scoring.
It was England's biggest win over Croatia and Croatia's heaviest defeat.
Croatia were coached by Slaven Bilic and led by Luka Modric, and Alex Scott started for England for the first time.
background: England and Croatia met in the 2018 World Cup semi-final, which Croatia won, so this result closed an old score.

headline: Kane equals Shilton's England appearance record in a 3-0 win over Czechia
facts: Kane reached 125 caps, level with Peter Shilton, in England's 3-0 home win over Czechia, scoring twice and adding an assist.
He has played in all but one of England's last 101 competitive matches, the exception being the 2024 Nations League loss to Greece.
ESPN later reports he became the outright record holder against Croatia at Wembley on 12 November.
background: Kane made his England debut at 21 and the article notes the only big gap in his career is a major trophy, as England's last was in 1966.

headline: Tuchel leaves Cole Palmer out of England squad, says he misses too many chances to impress
facts: Palmer and Kobbie Mainoo were left out for the Croatia and Spain games after withdrawing from the previous camp.
Tuchel said he rewards commitment in camp, that Palmer misses too many opportunities to impress him, and that the door stays open.
Jobe Bellingham and 19-year-old Josh King were called up.
background: Palmer is a Chelsea forward who has been a regular in England squads under Tuchel since early 2025, and Jobe joins his older brother Jude in the squad.

headline: Tuchel upset as anti-racism protocol questions overshadow England trip to Madrid
facts: After beating Croatia, Tuchel was asked how he would react to racist abuse in Spain and said he would remind players of the protocols.
Spain coach de la Fuente told a journalist there is no racism in Spain, and Tuchel said his message had been twisted and he was a little upset.
It was England's first visit to Madrid since 2004, a match marked by racist abuse of Black England players.
background: Spain were fined and had part of a stadium closed last month over Islamophobic chanting at a March friendly against Egypt in Barcelona.
footage_terms: Tuchel anti-racism protocol Spain press conference
Declan Rice England Madrid press conference

headline: England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid with ten men, ending Spain's 43-game unbeaten run
facts: Kane (penalty), Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored for England, while Oyarzabal (penalty) and Nico Williams scored for Spain.
Elliot Anderson was sent off in the 63rd minute for a last-man foul on Lamine Yamal and goalkeeper James Trafford made late saves.
Spain's coach de la Fuente said his side was overwhelmed early and called England exceptional.
background: Spain came into the match as World Cup and European champions, unbeaten in 43 competitive games over three years.

headline: UEFA hands England a suspended away-ticket ban after fans' chants in Madrid
facts: UEFA gave England a one-match away ticket sales ban, suspended for two years, plus a 12,600 pound fine.
Sky Sports News reported the sanction followed anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chanting in Madrid.
The FA condemned the chanting and said it would work with police to identify those responsible.
background: England fans have been disciplined by UEFA for chanting before, and this sanction is suspended rather than immediate.

headline: Tuchel says he will stay with England until Euro 2028 but wants a club job afterwards
facts: Tuchel has no release clause in the contract he signed in February and says he would turn down a big club approach before Euro 2028.
He says he misses the matchday rhythm of club football and plans to return to a club after England.
The story broke as Pochettino reportedly agreed in principle to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United.
background: Tuchel has coached Chelsea, Bayern Munich and PSG, and led England to the World Cup semi-finals this summer.

headline: Nations League quarter-final draw: England face Haaland's Norway, Spain meet France
facts: England meet Norway, Spain meet France, Netherlands meet holders Portugal and Belgium meet Jurgen Klopp's Germany.
The quarter-finals are played 25-30 March and the finals, including the 13 June decider, are 9-13 June 2027.
Tuchel called the Nations League useful Euros preparation and said the immediate goal is winning the quarter-final.
background: The England v Norway tie repeats the World Cup quarter-final that ESPN says England won 2-1, and Spain v France repeats the World Cup semi-final.
footage_terms: Spain France World Cup semi-final highlights

headline: England striker Ivan Toney fails to move assault trial away from Euro 2028
facts: Toney, 30, denies assault occasioning actual bodily harm over an alleged incident at a London nightclub on 6 December.
His trial is set for 12 June 2028, three days into Euro 2028, and the judge refused a request to move it to August.
The judge said the application can be renewed if Toney makes the England squad.
background: Toney is an England striker who was charged by the Metropolitan Police in late July.

headline: Juan Mata retires at 38 with a World Cup, Euros, Champions League and FA Cup
facts: Mata announced his retirement in a video on X, saying love sometimes means letting go.
He won the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 with Spain, the 2012 Champions League and FA Cup with Chelsea, and the 2016 FA Cup and 2017 Europa League with United.
His last two seasons were in Australia with Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.
background: Mata made 285 appearances for Manchester United between 2014 and 2022 and co-founded the Common Goal charity initiative in 2017.
footage_terms: Juan Mata best goals Chelsea Manchester United

headline: Zidane calls reports of a rift with Mbappe 'nonsense'
facts: Reports claimed Mbappe was unhappy playing on the left in September while Dembele played centrally and that the two barely talked.
Zidane called the reports nonsense and annoying, and described their relationship as strictly professional and working well.
Mbappe missed the 3-1 loss to Italy with a hamstring problem but was expected to be available against Turkiye.
background: Zidane replaced Didier Deschamps as France coach after the 2026 World Cup, and Mbappe won the Golden Boot at that tournament with 10 goals, per Wikipedia.

headline: Italy beat France 3-1 at San Siro, first home win over them since 1962, handing Zidane his first loss
facts: Pio Esposito scored twice, the second a 75th-minute penalty, and Davide Frattesi added a goal; Michael Olise scored for France.
His brother Sebastiano missed a penalty earlier, and Pio said he felt pressure to make people forget it.
Mbappe was missing, and it was Zidane's first defeat in five games as France coach.
background: Pio Esposito, 21, is an Inter striker who was on loan at Serie B Spezia until the start of last season, and Italy missed a third straight World Cup after a shootout loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

headline: Germany rout the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin to win their group, with Wirtz scoring twice
facts: Wirtz scored twice (60', 71'), with Scherhant, Schlotterbeck and Gruda also scoring in Berlin.
Germany needed a win by at least five goals to top Group A2 and did exactly that, with three goals in an 11-minute spell.
It was Germany's last match in an Adidas kit before the switch to Nike.
background: Klopp is in his first national-team job and Germany are now paired with Belgium in the Nations League quarter-finals.

headline: Haaland scores a 96th-minute penalty as Norway come from 0-2 down to beat Denmark 3-2
facts: Denmark led 2-0 within 15 minutes through Hojlund and Hojbjerg; Haaland scored before halftime, Odegaard equalised in the 87th minute.
VAR awarded a penalty for a handball by Joachim Andersen and Haaland converted at 95:45, his latest goal for Norway.
Haaland has 68 international goals and 25 in the Nations League, and he was booked for taking his shirt off.
background: Haaland is Norway's all-time top scorer and plays for Manchester City.

headline: Vinicius scores a hat-trick as Brazil beat Singapore 7-0, Ancelotti watches from the stands
facts: Vinicius scored in the 9th, 15th and 21st minutes, and Endrick, Estevao and Rayan also scored in a 7-0 friendly win.
Ancelotti watched from the stands because of a red card he got in Brazil's 3-2 loss to Japan.
It was Ancelotti's biggest win since he took charge in May 2025, against a Singapore side ranked 148th.
background: Ancelotti, the Italian coach who won five Champions Leagues, took over Brazil in May 2025.

headline: Estevao struggles at Chelsea under Xabi Alonso while Ancelotti keeps starting him for Brazil
facts: In 10 Premier League games this season Estevao has started only once, a 2-0 win over Manchester United.
Alonso prefers a 3-4-3 system that suits him badly, and Palmer and Rogers are ahead of him in the pecking order.
He has five Brazil goals, but his form dipped in the 3-2 loss to Japan, and Alonso says Chelsea have no plans to sell him.
background: He chose Chelsea over offers from Real Madrid and Barcelona, and a hamstring injury kept him out of the World Cup, per ESPN.

headline: Socceroos lose 0-2 to Jordan in Doha after the game is moved over security fears, Popovic's future in doubt
facts: The friendly was moved from Amman to Doha after Socceroos players raised security concerns following DFAT advice.
Patrick Beach saved a penalty from Al-Taamari, who then scored; Arzani was sent off and Ali Olwan added a second.
Popovic called the first half very poor, and it is unclear whether he will stay on after the team returns in March.
background: Australia had beaten Qatar 3-0 the week before and the squad now breaks until March.

headline: Ecuadorian player banned eight years for throwing a stone that broke a referee's cheekbone
facts: On 17 October a third-tier match ended with Perlaza throwing a stone at an assistant referee, who suffered a fractured cheekbone and needed surgery.
The federation banned him until 19 October 2034 and will ask FIFA to extend it worldwide.
The club was fined 2,000 dollars, must pay 4,369.73 dollars in medical costs and must play three home games at a neutral venue.
background: The player is 30 and played for Club Ciudad de Yantzaza in Ecuador's third tier, and the club said he is no longer a member.

headline: Oviedo fan gets a suspended prison sentence for racist abuse of Mbappe
facts: The fan received a suspended 11-month sentence, a stadium ban and a fine for a hate crime during the 24 August 2025 match at the Carlos Tartiere.
The prison term is suspended on condition he stays away from official football stadiums for two years.
LaLiga reported the incident and Real Madrid acted as private prosecutor, citing earlier convictions at four other stadiums.
background: Mbappe scored twice in Real Madrid's 3-0 win in that match.

headline: Emi Martinez returns for Argentina in a protective mask after jaw surgery
facts: Martinez, now Chelsea's goalkeeper, collided with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite on 16 October and had jaw surgery.
Alonso kept him out of the 8 November Sunderland game, calling an earlier return too rash and too risky.
Scaloni confirmed he would play against Costa Rica in the mask, and Martinez posted video of himself training in it.
background: Martinez was Argentina's goalkeeper in their World Cup win in 2022 and is now at Chelsea, per ESPN.
footage_terms: Emiliano Martinez jaw injury Chelsea Everton

headline: Arsenal teen Max Dowman, 16, becomes England's youngest U21 goalscorer
facts: Dowman scored a late tap-in winner in England U21's 3-2 win over France at Ashton Gate.
England had lost a two-goal lead, and the match came three days after a 1-0 loss to Portugal.
ESPN links the goal to his earlier record as England's youngest U21 player, which broke Jude Bellingham's mark.
background: Dowman is a 16-year-old Arsenal player and is part of England's U21 preparation for next year's European Championship.
